intended_object: The universal point of the standard affine chart of the Grassmannian at x: the universal R-linear map ψ : M → B^k, where B is the coordinate ring of the chart (Sym_R(M^k) modulo the relations ψ(x_i) = e_i). The j-th component sends m to the class of the generator (0,…,m,…,0) in position j. This comes from the docstring and from how the library uses it in `homEquiv`/`chartHomEquiv`.
explanation:
`ChartAlgebra R x` is Sym_R(M^k) divided by the ideal generated by ι(single j (x i)) − δ_ij. The definition builds the linear map M → (ChartAlgebra R x)^k one component at a time. Its j-th component is m ↦ [ι(Pi.single j m)], which is exactly what the docstring describes.

This map is the universal element of the corepresented functor: `universalLinearMap_apply_self` shows that it sends x_i to e_i. `homEquiv` then identifies an algebra map g : ChartAlgebra → A with the map ψ obtained by applying g to each coordinate of this universal map. So it is the tautological point of the affine chart. That chart is a genuine object of algebraic geometry, the universal family over the open cell of the Grassmannian.

Generality: R is any commutative ring and M is any module. The index type Fin k is built into the rank-k Grassmannian setup used throughout the library, so it does not make the definition too narrow. Mathlib has no counterpart for Grassmannian charts or their universal points.
